question: How do the server, the page and the desktop shell fit together?
tldr: One Node server per project; page and desktop shell talk to it.
answer: The server owns files, git, the index, terminals and the chat, and pushes changes over an event stream. The Svelte page renders them; the Rust window only starts servers and hosts the page.
why: Three processes and several channels (HTTP, an event stream, WebSockets) are not obvious from the files.

nodes.label: Desktop shell
nodes.tldr: GTK window, one server per project
nodes.explain: Starts a server on a free port per project, shows the page in WebKitGTK and stops the servers on close.

nodes.label: Svelte page
nodes.explain: The UI built by Vite; its state lives in one reactive store fed by the event stream.

nodes.label: Node server
nodes.tldr: Owns the project's data and agents
nodes.explain: Serves the page, a JSON API, an event stream and WebSockets for terminals and language servers.

nodes.label: Token gate
nodes.tldr: Only the page with the token gets in
nodes.explain: Every request and WebSocket needs the server's token (a cookie, set from the link the desktop app or the server's output gives) and, on loopback, a loopback Host: a site pointing its own name at 127.0.0.1 gets nowhere.

nodes.label: Event stream
nodes.explain: Server-sent events: the full state on connect, then only the lists that changed.

nodes.label: Git
nodes.tldr: Status and diffs, asked side by side
nodes.explain: git runs as async child processes (src/git.ts), in parallel, so a large repo doesn't stall the terminals and the chat stream that share the server's thread.

nodes.label: Code index
nodes.tldr: Modules and items the links name
nodes.explain: The skeleton of the code (packages, modules, items), rebuilt in the background when sources change.

nodes.label: Agent chat
nodes.tldr: Agent SDK sessions, several at once
nodes.explain: Runs Claude Code with the user's login, one process per conversation that is working, and streams the open conversation's items to the page (the others only as working / waiting for you).

nodes.label: Terminals
nodes.explain: Shells whose commands, folder and exit codes are tracked, attached over a WebSocket.

nodes.label: Project folder and git
nodes.explain: The working tree the agent edits and the server watches.

nodes.label: Claude Code login
nodes.explain: Cockpit uses it through the SDK; no API key.
